{{nihongo|'''Tsumatsuhime Shrine'''|都麻都比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

As the company name suggests, it is said to be a shrine that enshrines '''{{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|Q10935047|qid=Q10935047|lt=Tsumatsuhime}}''' (Tsumatsuhime no Mikoto, Sakutsuhime no Mikoto) as its enshrined deity.Regarding Tsumatsuhime, it is described in one book in "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}" that she is the daughter god of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo}}. Also, the older brother god of Tsumatsuhime is {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru/Itakeru}}, and the older sister god is {{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|Q10935047|qid=Q10935047|lt=Oyatsuhime no Mikoto}} ( Both gods are enshrined at {{ill|Itakiso shrine|Q11379271|qid=Q11379271}} (Itaikiso, Wakayama City) and {{ill|Oyatsuhime Shrine|Q11434556|qid=Q11434556}} (Udamori, Wakayama City), respectively. These three deities are said to be the gods who brought tree species to Kii Province, and in Kii they are collectively known as ``''Itaiki Sosanjin'' {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}.

The first reference to the historical material is the article in "{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ar|شوكو نيهونغي|ca|Shoku Nihongi|cs|Šoku Nihongi|de|Shoku Nihongi|es|Shoku Nihongi|eu|Shoku Nihongi|fa|شوکو نیهونگی|ff|Shoku Nihongi|fr|Shoku Nihongi|id|Shoku Nihongi|it|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|ko|속일본기|ms|Shoku Nihongi|pt|Shoku Nihongi|ru|Сёку нихонги|simple|Shoku Nihongi|sl|Šoku Nihongi|th|โชกุนิฮงงิ|tr|Shoku Nihongi|uk|Сьоку Ніхонґі|zh|續日本紀|qid=Q611399}}" {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} 2nd year ({{ill|702|Q23497|qid=Q23497}})<ref group="original">"Shoku Nihongi" article dated February 22, 702. In </ref>, there is an article about the separation of the three shrines of Ita-Kiso, Oya-Tohime, and Toma-Tohime.{{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}.

"Shinsho Kaku Chofusho" {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daido}} 1st year ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}})<ref group="原">"Shinsho Kakuchofusho" 10 (Shinji Shoke Fudo) Daido 1st year (806). In </ref>, 13 houses were given to ``Tomazuhime no Kami'' of Kii Province {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}. Related, {{ill|Jōhei|Q1324874|qid=Q1324874|lt=Shohei}} ({{ill|931|Q24789|qid=Q24789}}-{{ill|938|Q24794|qid=Q24794}}) "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Japanese name Ruijusho}}', ``Tsuma (Tsuma) Go'' is seen in Kii Province {{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}}, which is said to mean ``Tsuma Kobe'' {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}.As {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}, {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan}} In the first year of the year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), he was promoted to the lower rank of Jushii (junior fourth rank) as ``Shinto Matsuhime'' along with Itagesojin and Ōyatsuhime no kami {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}.

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}} 5 years ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} states that in Nagusa District, Kii Province, there are "Tomatohime Shrine Meishindai It will be listed at {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} as ``Monthly New Year'' and {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}} and {{jalink| It is written that it was kept in {{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}} at Niinamesai|Q11501518}}{{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}. In ``{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}'', the Tenjin is listed as ``Junior Fourth Rank Upper Tumatsu Hime Okami'', and it is different from Itaukeso Okami, who rose to Shoichi Rank (Shoichi Rank), and has an open shrine {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}. In addition, in the same book, there is also a related entry of ``Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Tsumutohime no Okami.''

Its subsequent history is unclear, and there are various theories as to which shrine the above shrine belongs to.

=== Historical evidence ===
The exact location of Shikinai Shrine ``Tomatsu Hime Shrine'' is still uncertain. In ancient times, it is identified as Miyako Matsuhime Shrine (Kichirei, (1)) in Shandong in the "Kiokuni Famous Places Zue" and "Nanki Shrine Record" ({{ill|Enkyō (Edo period)|Q1183728|qid=Q1183728}}3 ({{ill|1746|Q7589|qid=Q7589}})).

Furthermore, in ``{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}'', it is said that Matsuhime Shrine (1), the capital of Shandong, which is mentioned in ``Nanki Shrine Roku'', was originally dedicated to ``Yoshire Tsuhime no Mikoto'' {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}. Yoshiretsuhime-no-Mikoto appears in the ``Kiokuni Jinmyocho'' as ``Junior Fifth Rank Lower, Yoshiretsu Hime-no-Kami.'' In addition, in "Zoku Fudoki", there is a theory that Hirao's wife Daimyo Shrine (currently Tomatohime Shrine, (2)) is referred to as ``Toumatsuhime Shrine'' {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}.

One of these theories is that {{ill|Water conflict|Q2464727|qid=Q2464727}} ({{ill|Water theory of Szene-Kunikake Shrine and Kodaimyojin|Q11504966|qid=Q11504966}}) that occurred between {{ill|Hinokuma Shrine|Q888184|qid=Q888184}} and Wasaso. |Q1193059}}5 ({{ill|1433|Q6356|qid=Q6356}}) states that Takazumi Shrine (3) was originally located in Maemiya, and later moved its enshrined place to Shandong, and later to Mt. Wasa.{{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}. Since this legend is consistent with an article written in 702 in the ``Shoku Nihongi'', ``Zoku Fudoki'' states that there is a high possibility that Takazumi Shrine is Tomatohime Shrine {{Sfn|Takazumi Shrine (Taira)|1983}}.

=== History ===
{{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} "Tomatsu Hime Shrine" in {{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}. This is compared to our company in "Ki Province Meisho Zue" and "Nanki Shrine Record" ({{ill|Enkyō (Edo period)|Q1183728|qid=Q1183728}}3 ({{ill|1746|Q7589|qid=Q7589}})). On the other hand, "Zoku Fudoki" denies this, and our company says that it is a shrine that enshrines the "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Yoshiretsuhime-no-kami" that appears in the "Kiokuni Jinmyocho", and compares Matsumatsuhime-kami to Takazumi Shrine.

According to the shrine statement book, our company was dedicated as Shikinai Shrine ``Miyatomatsuhime Shrine'' during the Edo period, but in {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} it was renamed to ``Yoshiretsuhime Shrine'' {{Sfn|Miyatomatsu Hime Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987|p=51-52}}. In the 6th year of the Meiji era ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked as {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} in the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=old shrine rank}}. After that, in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}21 ({{ill|1946|Q18610|qid=Q18610}}), it reverted to its former name ``Miyakomatsuhime Shrine'' and remains the current name.

'''Tsumatsu Hime Shrine'' (Tsumatsu Hime Jinja, Miyako Mazu Hime Shrine) is located in {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}{{ill|Wakayama (city)|Q200747|qid=Q200747}}Hirao. {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}) {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}. {{Sfn|Tomatsu Hime Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine) |1987|p=51-52}} adjacent to the ruins of Heioji Shrine on the Kumano Kodo.

=== Enshrined God ===
* {{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|Q10935047|qid=Q10935047|lt=Miyakomatsuhime no Mikoto}}

=== History ===
{{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} "Tomatsu Hime Shrine" in {{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}. In ``Zoku Fudoki'', there is a theory that compares the company to this, and in addition, there is a theory that compares it to ``Junior Fourth Rank Lower, Tsumatsuhiba Okami'' in the ``Kiokuni Jinmyocho'' {{Sfn|Hirao Village (Taira)|1983}}.

The company name is ``Tsumadaimyo Shrine'' in ``Zoku Fudoki,'' and ``Tsuma Gozen Shrine'' in ``Kiokuni Meisho Zue.'' According to "Zoku Fudoki", the precincts were once two and a half towns and the shrine building was majestic, but it fell into disrepair during the Tensho War, and although it was revived by {{ill|Toyotomi Hidenaga|Q1191183|qid=Q1191183}}, it declined. Currently, a small shrine is enshrined in the precincts of about 6 steps. Two stone lanterns dating back to {{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}}5 ({{ill|1740|Q7006|qid=Q7006}}) stand in the shrine grounds.

Furthermore, according to "Kanei-ki", it is said that on the first day of the New Year, the first day of the Pig in October, and the first day of the New Year in November, members of the shrine of Ita-keiso Shrine once served the company.
